optionReasons.saa-ini-171:option:1: The GuardDuty detects threats by analyzing logs (CloudTrail, VPC Flow, DNS) — it doesn't scan software packages in search of CVEs.
optionReasons.saa-ini-171:option:2: The Trusted Advisor Basic brings limited checks of good practice — does not scan software vulnerabilities.
optionReasons.saa-ini-171:option:3: The AWS Config assesses the CONFIGURATION of remedies against rules — does not inspect installed packages.

finalJustifications: Because Inspector automatic scanning and continuous instances EC2 and images in ECR in search of VECs and network exposure, with priority risk report.
Because Inspector automatically blocks malicious traffic on the edge of the network, preventing the exploitation of the CVEs found.
Because Inspector encrypts vulnerable container images in ECR, isolating them until a corrected version is published.
Because Inspector apply the patches of VECs alone in the instances, using the Systems Manager to correct without intervention.

optionReasons.saa-ini-092:option:1: The QuickSight is generic BI — you would have to mount datasets and dashboards; the Cost Explorer already delivers the cost analysis ready.
optionReasons.saa-ini-092:option:2: The Trusted Advisor recommends optimizations — is not a graphical analysis tool of the expense history.
optionReasons.saa-ini-092:option:3: The CloudTrail audit calls from API — does not analyze costs.

finalJustifications: Because Cost Explorer brings interactive graphs of cost history with filters and clusters by service, tag and period, including trend analysis.
Because Cost Explorer issues the consolidated monthly tax note of the account, with the items grouped by service and project tag.
Because Cost Explorer apply automatic discounts when identifying waste, adjusting the invoice according to the usage trend.
Because Cost Explorer automatically closes the idle resources you find, containing the growth of the analyzed expenses.

optionReasons.saa-ini-093:option:1: Computer Optimizer recommends resource sizing — does not issue budget alerts.
optionReasons.saa-ini-093:option:2: The CUR is the gross and detailed report of use and cost for analysis — it does not trigger threshold alerts.
optionReasons.saa-ini-093:option:3: The Inspector is vulnerability scanner — nothing to do with financial control.

finalJustifications: Because AWS Budgets allows setting a budget with alerts on spending thresholds REAL (80%) and PREVISTO (overhang), by notifying by e-mail or SNS.
Because Budgets blocks the account automatically when reaching the defined ceiling, preventing the development environment from spending more.
Because Budgets renegotiates the prices of services with the AWS when the month's expenditure is close to the established budget.
Because Budgets requires Savings Plans assets in the account: it is the usage commitments that feed the overrun forecast.

optionReasons.saa-ini-097:option:0: User IAM identifies credentials of persons — resource costs are not attributed to the person who created them.
optionReasons.saa-ini-097:option:1: Manual spreadsheet process is slow, prone to error and does not integrate with cost tools of AWS.
optionReasons.saa-ini-097:option:3: The name of the instance does not appear as a cost dimension in the billing.

finalJustifications: Because cost allocation tags, after activated in Billing, saw filter dimensions in Cost Explorer and no CUR — enabling the view of expenditure by project and department.
Because tags reduce the price of tagged resources: a AWS grants categorization discount, reflected in billing reports.
Because Billing requires standardized tags to issue the consolidated invoice — without them, costs do not appear in monthly reports.
Because tags automatically move each project's resources to separate accounts, isolating department billing in the organization.

optionReasons.saa-ini-098:option:0: There is no age exemption from the account — data transfer collection is permanent.
optionReasons.saa-ini-098:option:1: It's the opposite: ENTRADA data is usually free — the AWS does not charge to receive your data.
optionReasons.saa-ini-098:option:2: Exit to the Internet and traffic between AZs and Regions ARE charged — not all transfers are free of charge.

finalJustifications: Because data entry is usually free and the charge falls on the Internet exit and traffic between AZs and Regions — flows that an optimized architecture minimizes.
Because the AWS charge only data input transfer, a mechanism that compensates for the cost of free output storage.
Because all traffic within the same Region is free, including between AZs — the charge exists only in communication between Regions.
Because the transfer cost is a monthly fixed value per account, regardless of volume — optimizing the flow does not change the bill at the end of the month.

optionReasons.saa-ini-100:option:0: The CloudFormation provide infrastructure as code — does not audit costs or identify waste.
optionReasons.saa-ini-100:option:2: The GuardDuty detects security threats — does not identify financial waste.
optionReasons.saa-ini-100:option:3: X-Ray tracks distributed requests to debug performance — nothing to do with costs.

finalJustifications: Because Trusted Advisor brings ready cost checks — underutilized instances, volumes EBS orphans, elastic idle IPs and reserve opportunities — with actionable recommendations.
Because Trusted Advisor Automatically disconnect the idle features you find — instances, volumes and IPs are released without manual approval.
Because Trusted Advisor grants credits back from wasted resources, compensating in the invoice the cost of the identified idleness.
Because Trusted Advisor analyzes only accounts with Basic support plan, the entry category where cost optimization is most critical.

optionReasons.saa-ini-153:option:0: Xeon's previous generation may cost less, but it doesn't offer the best cost-performance ratio — and the question asks the chip developed by itself AWS.
optionReasons.saa-ini-153:option:1: Spot is a MODELO OF COMPRA (at risk of interruption), not a processor family — and does not take advantage of compatibility ARM64.
optionReasons.saa-ini-153:option:2: GPUs (G/P families) accelerate specific loads such as ML and graphics, cost expensive and do not benefit from compilation or generic microservices.

finalJustifications: Because Graviton is the processor ARM developed by itself AWS, available in families such as M6g/C6g/R6g, with better cost-performance for loads compatible with ARM64.
Because Graviton emulates the x86 with identical performance in any application, exempting any recompilation of the code to ARM64.
Because Graviton instances are free in the first year of use, the discount of the launch of the AWS to popularize architecture ARM.
Because Graviton is a dedicated compiler: download the builds from CPU main, as a GPU makes with graphics.

optionReasons.saa-ini-181:option:0: On-Demand is exactly the full price that the team wants to reduce — there is no discount.
optionReasons.saa-ini-181:option:1: Spot gives the biggest discount, but can be interrupted by AWS at any time — unacceptable for a database 24/7.
optionReasons.saa-ini-181:option:3: Dedicated Hosts meet licensing/compliance requirements and cost MAIS, Not less.

finalJustifications: Because the Reserved Instances exchange a commitment of 1 or 3 years for discounts up to ~75% on On-Demand — ideal for stable, predictable and continuous loading.
Because the RIs move the instance to dedicated redundant hardware, leaving it immune to hardware failures during the contract.
Because the RIs include the Enterprise support plan at no additional cost during the entire commitment period.
Because RIs allow you to hibernate the instance without losing data, paying only storage in periods of inactivity.
